rounds.text: H. S. India Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.54x [E2] and a P/E of 10.2x [E1], both of which are substantially lower than their respective sector benchmarks of 2.28x and 26.12x [E6, E7]. The company has demonstrated a strong turnaround in performance, evidenced by a 26% compounded profit growth over five years [E19] and a 131% year-over-year net profit increase [E56, E60]. This profitability is backed by high-quality cash flow, with a cash conversion ratio of 2.85x and operating cash flow representing 122% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Furthermore, the company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing borrowings from Rs 16.27 Cr to Rs 12.43 Cr [E39, E49]. Conceded: the company has a low return on equity of 4.65% over the last three years [E52], does not pay a dividend [E4, E51], and has experienced a 19% decline in share price over the last year [E25]. Despite these headwinds, the current market price implies a negative earnings growth expectation, which stands in stark contrast to the company's recent fundamental outperformance [E45, E46].
